title: Linear Diophantine equations
section: Part A: Number Theory ▷ The Diophantine Equation ax + by = c
terms: Diophantine equation; integer solution; linear Diophantine equation; Fermat last theo- rem.

exposition.text:
A Diophantine equation seeks solutions in integers, sometimes with additional positivity restric-
tions. For ab ̸= 0 and d = gcd(a, b), ax + by = c is solvable in integers exactly when d | c. If
(x , y ) is one solution, all solutions are x = x + (b/d)t, y = y − (a/d)t, with t ∈ Z.
0 0 0 0
Obtain one solution from Bezout’s identity multiplied by c/d, then impose bounds on the in-
teger parameter. The same parametrization applies when c = 0; one may use (0, 0) as the
particular solution. Higher-degree Diophantine equations can behave very differently: Fermat’s
n n n
last theorem says x + y = z has no nonzero integer solution for integer n > 2.
The homogeneous equation uses the primitive direction (b/d, −a/d), not (b, −a) unless d = 1.
2 2
Bounds or an objective such as x + y are imposed after parametrizing; a quadratic objective
reduces to checking integers nearest its real minimizer. Clearing a common denominator trans-
fers a rational power equation to an integer one, allowing Fermat's theorem to rule out nonzero
rational solutions as well.

question.text:
How many pairs of nonnegative integers (x, y) satisfy 18x + 30y = 252?
(A) 2 (B) 3 (C) 4 (D) 5 (E) 6

solution.text:
Divide by 6: 3x + 5y = 42. Modulo 3, y ≡ 0, so y = 3t and x = 14 − 5t. Nonnegativity
permits exactly t = 0, 1, 2, yielding three pairs.

question.text:
What is the least positive integer x for which there exists an integer y satisfying 26x + 39y = 65?
(A) 1 (B) 2 (C) 3 (D) 4 (E) 5

solution.text:
Divide by 13 to get 2x + 3y = 5. Modulo 3, 2x ≡ 2, hence x ≡ 1 (mod 3). The least positive
choice is x = 1, and then y = 1.

question.text:
Which parametrization gives all integer solutions of 12x + 18y = 0, with t ranging over all
integers?
(A) (x, y) = (18t, −12t) (B) (x, y) = (3t, −2t)
(C) (x, y) = (2t, −3t) (D) (x, y) = (3t, 2t)
(E) (x, y) = (t, −t)

solution.text:
Divide by six to obtain 2x + 3y = 0. Since two and three are coprime, 3 | x; write x = 3t,
which forces y = −2t. The first parametrization gives only every sixth solution and is in-
complete. Here t ranges over all integers.

How many ordered pairs of rational numbers (u, v) satisfy u + v = 1?
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) Infinitely many

solution.text:
If both rational numbers are nonzero, use a common positive denominator d to write u =

rem. If one is zero, the other is one, giving exactly (0, 1) and (1, 0).

Among integer solutions of 7x + 11y = 1, what is the minimum of x + y ?
(A) 5 (B) 10 (C) 13 (D) 25 (E) 34

solution.text:
One solution is (−3, 2), and all are x = −3+11t, y = 2−7t for integer t. The squared norm is

170t − 94t + 13, whose real minimum occurs at 47/170. The nearest integer is zero; checking
the two adjacent integers confirms the minimum 13 at t = 0.

For how many integers k with 1 ≤ k ≤ 100 does 28x + 42y = k + 3 have an integer solution?
(A) 7 (B) 12 (C) 14 (D) 16 (E) 28

solution.text:
2
The gcd of the coefficients is fourteen, so solvability requires k + 3 ≡ 0 (mod 14). Modulo
seven this means k ≡ ±2, and modulo two it requires k odd. Combining gives k ≡ 5 or
9 (mod 14). The first ninety-eight integers contain seven complete blocks, giving fourteen
values; ninety-nine and one hundred add none.
